text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming (region: us-west-2). Elevated tail and streaming stalls. Metric spike started ~1m ago. Auto-mitigation: enabled soft-throttles on background prefill jobs.
Marta: saw it, thanks. p95 also drifting up but p99 is the killer. Any customer-facing errors?
Ryan: one customer support ticket from AcmeInc for partial streams timing out ~8s. Not widespread 5xxs, mostly high tail and stalled chunks.
Kai: looking at kv-cache metrics now — shard set s12 and s13 show rapid eviction + growing slab fragmentation. Prefill backlog is growing on decode workers.
Eli: hmm prefill vs decode imbalance again? Are we prefetching too aggressively for some prefixes?
Marta: that's my read. Prefill queue length ~3x normal for the last 90s. decode workers CPU ok, but disk paging on some nodes spiked.
Ryan: attaching quick trace snippets: ```
span: rpc/recv -> 210ms
span: kv:prefill -> 1.2s
span: kv:decode -> 80ms
span: stream/chunk -> stall 6.4s
```
Kai: that matches prefill taking the hit, causing streaming tail stalls while decode waits for KV page-ins.
Eli: any recent deploys? deploy-bot: show last deploy.
deploy-bot: last deployment: service/runtime v3.9.12 by ops-ci at 1763499500, no schema changes; config flag kv.prefill.enabled=true unchanged.
Marta: OK no recent config flips. We need a short mitigation: reduce prefill aggressiveness and increase slab safety margin on impacted shards, and temporarily raise streaming priority for decode paths.
Ryan: agree. Oncall runbook for kv-pressure suggests: 1) toggle kv.prefill.min_concurrency down, 2) bump slab retention for hot shards, 3) scale up nodes if pressure persists.
Kai: I'm on node ops. Running quick command to lower prefill concurrency on the us-west pool: ```bash
redwoodctl config set --scope=us-west kv.prefill.min_concurrency=2
redwoodctl rollout restart service/runtime --filter region=us-west
```
Marta: do it, but roll it can cause in-flight stalls. Kai, prefer a staged config push to control impact.
Kai: pushing to 2 with a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) now. Watching telemetry.
Eli: while that's rolling, I'll bump slab retention for shards s12,s13 (target ratio +0.15). Command: ```bash
redwoodctl kv slab-tune --shard s12 --delta 0.15
redwoodctl kv slab-tune --shard s13 --delta 0.15
```
Eli: ran both. new target applied. Should reduce eviction churn and paging.
Ryan: telemetry update?
oncall-bot: telemetry: prefill queue length falling (was 3x -> 1.1x). p99 for /v1/streaming decreased from 4.8s -> 1.1s over last 30s. Error rate stable.
Marta: getting customer update ready: AcmeInc affected for ~90s with timeouts on long streams. We'll message them: short blip, mitigation in place, will follow up with RCA. Ryan can you draft?
Ryan: draft: "We observed a transient tail latency spike caused by KV cache pressure and prefill imbalance. We applied config changes to reduce prefill concurrency and tuned slab retention on impacted shards which restored streaming performance. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline and prevention plan." Publish?
Marta: yes. add: "No data loss; some streams experienced partial stalls/timeouts" and send to CSM.
Ryan: sent to CSM and posted to #customer-notify.
Kai: rolling status: staged config at 10% passed, 50% passed, 100% done. No retries.
Eli: slab-tune logs show reduced eviction rate and lower page-in latency on s12/s13.
Marta: ok closing outage? Do we want to keep an eye for 30m before closing?
SRE-Team: +1 on 30m watch. Create follow-up ticket to root cause: investigate why prefill backlog built up (prefix distribution change? model change? traffic spike?).
Marta: created ticket SRE-1347: "Investigate prefill vs decode imbalance and slab fragmentation leading to streaming tail latency" and assigned to Kai/Eli. ETA EOD.
Ryan: I'll annotate incident timeline and link metrics/dashboards.
Marta: thanks all. If p99 creeps up again, escalate to infra and consider emergency node scale-up. For now mark as mitigated and monitor. :thumbsup:
